title: Water transportation and water treatment plant maintenance at ALMA Observatory.
description: Division: DOO. Preliminary Inquiry (PI) to identify and select companies that are interested in and capable to provide maintenance services for the water treatment plant and water transportation services for the ALMA Observatory, located close to San Pedro de Atacama, Chile. The scope of the services includes 2 lots: Lot 1: Water transportation services, including: - Transportation of potable water required for the operation of the Observatory from Calama and/or San Pedro de Atacama. - Transportation of Industrial water from Calama and/or San Pedro de Atacama to the Observatory. Lot 2: Water treatment plant maintenance, including: - Operation and maintenance of the water treatment plant. - Sanitising of water storage tanks. - Corrective maintenance of the potable water distribution pipes and wastewater pipes. - Extraction from pits, sludge removal, cleaning of grease chambers, supply and cleaning of chemical toilets. - Analysis of potable and waste water according to the norm Nch 409 and NCh 1333. - Testing and certification of sludge from the water treatment plant. The contract will start on the 1st of January 2021 for a firm period of 3 years, with the option to extend it by up to 2 more years. The Preliminary Inquiry is expected to be issued in Q1 2020 to potential suppliers in Chile, and will be followed by a Call for Tender that is scheduled to be released in Q2 2020. title: ARTES CC - ADVANCED TECHNOLOGY - WORK PLAN 2021 - EMITS / WEBSITE
description: A key role of ESA within the satellite telecommunications sector is to promote high levels of Research and Development activity within Participating State industry to help ensure both their preparedness and competitiveness in both the short and long terms. ARTESCore Competitiveness Element Programme Component "A" Advanced Technology (ARTES AT) is concerned with the early development stages ofnew systems and the exploitation of new and promising technologies for satellite communications. In some instances ARTES AT activities are a continuation of activities such as ARTES Future Preparations (ARTES FP) and the Technology Development Element (TDE). Through ARTES AT, ESA supports the introduction of new technologies into equipment designs so that in the long-term, industry will be able to introduce state-of-the-art equipment and (sub)systems at competitive prices to the commercial marketplace. ARTES AT encompasses activities related to the development of both (sub)systems and equipment for satellite communications.ARTES AT is the Agency's main programme for preparatory development of satellite communications technology. ARTES AT involves long-term RD activities inherently incorporating a significant level of technical risk, and is therefore fully funded by the Agency.A key role of ESA within the satellite telecommunications sector is to promote high levels of Research and Development activity within Participating State industry to help ensure both their preparedness and competitiveness in both the short and long terms.ARTES Core Competitiveness Element Programme Component "A" Advanced Technology (ARTES AT) is concerned with the early development stages of new systems and the exploitation of new and promising technologies for satellite communications. ARTES AT involves long-term RD activities inherently incorporating a significantlevel of technical risk, and is therefore fully funded by the Agency.The Work Plan for 2021 specifically addresses technology and equipment activities in support of the priorities defined in the Telecommunications Long Term Plan. The Work Plan for 2021 has been coordinated with other ESA technology programmes. The activities are organised per application area and grouped as Ground Segment, System, or Space segment (Payload, Platform) related. Activities identified as B will be issued according to the schedule published (and regularly updated) on the ESA ARTES web site: https://artes.esa.int/advanced-technology (ARTES 4.0 Planned Activities Summary Table). B activities for which industry and Participating States declare an interest will be given precedence when preparingInvitations To Tender (ITT).
